judged_text: save_host persists any staff-supplied category_id with no check that the category exists or is not read-restricted, while the embed read path performs no category-permission check, so the new per-host category mapping can point embedding at a private category. A staff member who maps an embeddable host to a read-restricted category causes topics imported from that host — and every reply posted to them in-forum — to be served by the anonymous EmbedController comments endpoint into the external embedding page (and to anyone forging a Referer), leaking restricted-category discussions off-site.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host blindly assigns `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (only defaulting to uncategorized when blank) with no check that the category exists or that it is not `read_restricted` (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb). It also shows TopicEmbed.import now uses the per-host category mapping (`category: eh.try(:category_id)`) instead of the removed `SiteSetting.embed_category` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), so a staff-configured private category could be selected. However, the finding’s core claim that the anonymous embed read path performs no category-permission check and therefore leaks private-category content is not verifiable from the provided diff (the embed controller rendering/authorization logic isn’t shown), so the off-site leak conclusion is speculative based on this diff alone.
